items.title: The name
items.text: Bought by Systemax in 2008, retired in 2012, used by a deals website from 2018.[^17][^19][^21] On October 8, 2026 compusa.com returned an error page.[^22] We could not establish who holds the trademark now.

items.title: The stores
items.text: Sixteen passed to Systemax in early 2008 and traded as CompUSA until the brand was dropped. Systemax closed 31 retail stores in 2015 and left the business.[^17][^20] The rest ran closing sales from December 2007.[^13]

items.title: The website
items.text: CompUSA.com went to Systemax for **$18.9M** with the intellectual property, and contributed to $226.3M of CompUSA sales in Systemax’s 2008 accounts.[^17]

items.title: Systemax’s consumer business
items.text: The TigerDirect operation that absorbed CompUSA was sold to PCM, Inc. on December 1, 2015 and the remainder wound down in 2016.[^20]

items.title: The owner’s bill
items.text: One 2007 report, citing The Wall Street Journal, put Carlos Slim’s total investment at about $2 billion.[^14] What the Gordon Brothers sale returned was not disclosed.[^13]

blocks.title: Who has owned the CompUSA name
blocks.subtitle: Five owners or users in four decades.

nodes.what: Formed in Dallas. Renamed CompUSA in March 1991 and listed that December.[^1][^8]
Tender offer for all the shares. América Móvil later reported a 49% interest.[^5][^6][^9]
Buys the company to sell or close the 103 stores, the web business and the service arm.[^13]
Buys the brand, trademarks, website and 16 store leases.[^16][^17]
A deals website relaunches compusa.com. TechSpot reported that it had bought the brand; terms were not disclosed.[^21]
The address returns an error page.[^22]
